Analise o(s) documento(s) de cenário do projeto e gere o SRS completo no formato especificado, seguindo o processo de trabalho: buscas dedicadas na base de conhecimento para cada tipo de artefato, rastreabilidade validada entre os artefatos.

Documento(s) de cenário:
--- Project Scenario 8.pdf ---
BECS (Book E-Commerce System)
So basically what we're trying to do is get books selling 
online instead of however you guys are doing it now, just a 
simple site where people can come in, look through what's 
available, throw a few books in a cart and check out. Nothing 
crazy, I just want it to actually work and not be a headache 
to keep up with. Right now I think it's all kind of manual or 
scattered and there's no real way for someone to just browse 
and buy without someone in the middle handling it, so that's 
the itch we're trying to scratch here. 
 
Anybody coming to the site should be able to just make an 
account, that's it, no big verification process or anything, 
and once they're in they can search for books and see title, 
author, price, add stuff to their cart and go through 
checkout. Keep the search simple, just matching on the title 
and it has to be exact, nothing fancy like partial matches or 
letting people search by author, that's more than we need 
right now. Some of these people might want to sign up to get 
notified about promotions and deals, so let's call those folks 
members, and they're the ones who can use promo codes when 
they check out. I picture this being pretty bare-bones in 
terms of who can buy what, like one copy of each book per 
order is plenty, we don't need people stacking ten copies of 
the same thing in their cart. 
 
On my side of things, I need a way to manage the inventory, 
basically a login that lets me add new books, edit prices, see 
how much stock I've got, that kind of stuff. I also want the 
system to ping me, like an email or something, whenever a book 
is running low so I don't get caught without stock, unless 
I've told it not to bother for that particular book because 
maybe I'm discontinuing it. And I want to be able to set up 
these percentage-off promotions every now and then and have it 
just email all the members automatically when I create one. 
 
One thing I want to be upfront about, we don't need to 
actually process real credit cards or handle real money 
movement right now, just collect the card number as part of 
the checkout flow and spit out a receipt and keep a log of 
what was purchased, who bought it, when. The real payment 
processing piece is something for way later, not part of this. 
Same with security stuff, I know that sounds bad, but honestly 
for what we need right now I'm not worried about encryption or 
people forgetting passwords or whatever, that's not a 
priority, let's not spend time building password recovery or 
anything like that for now. 
 
There's only going to be one person managing the store, me 
basically, so don't worry about building out roles for 
multiple managers or anything fancy like that, and a manager 
should never also be a regular customer account, those are two 
separate hats. It just needs to run somewhere people can get 
to it through a normal browser, nothing exotic on the 
technical side, just something stable that people in here can 
pull up and use without issues.

Sistema: BECS (Book E-Commerce System)

Resumo executivo: BECS is a browser-accessible e-commerce system that enables customers to independently browse and purchase books online, replacing the current manual or fragmented sales process. It provides catalog search, shopping cart, checkout, order records, membership promotions, and inventory and promotion administration for a single store manager.

Escopo: The system enables online book catalog browsing, ordering, membership promotions, and inventory administration through a web browser.
  Em escopo: Customer account registration and authentication
  Em escopo: Exact-title book search and catalog browsing
  Em escopo: Shopping cart and checkout with card-number collection
  Em escopo: Receipt generation and purchase logging
  Em escopo: Membership enrollment and promotional-code application
  Em escopo: Book inventory, price, stock, and low-stock notification management
  Em escopo: Percentage-off promotion creation and member email notifications
  Fora de escopo: Real credit-card authorization, charging, settlement, or money movement — explicitly deferred to a future release
  Fora de escopo: Password recovery — explicitly excluded from this release
  Fora de escopo: Account verification — registration must not require a verification process
  Fora de escopo: Partial-title and author-based search — explicitly not required for this release
  Fora de escopo: Multiple manager roles or manager-role administration — only one manager is expected
  Fora de escopo: Encryption requirements — explicitly not prioritized for this release
  Premissa: PA-01: Customers, members, and the store manager have access to a supported web browser.
  Premissa: PA-02: An email delivery capability is available to send low-stock and promotion notifications.
  Premissa: PA-03: The store manager is responsible for maintaining book, price, stock, notification, and promotion data.
  Restrição: REST-01 (Deployment): The system must be accessible through a standard web browser.
  Restrição: REST-02 (Organization): The system supports exactly one store manager account.
  Restrição: REST-03 (Payment): The system must not process real payments in this release.
  Restrição: REST-04 (Account segregation): A manager account must not also be a customer account.

Stakeholders:
  STK-01 - Customer (Usuário primário): Register an account, browse and search books, manage a cart, complete checkout, and receive a receipt.
  STK-02 - Member (Usuário primário): Receive promotion notifications and apply promotional codes during checkout.
  STK-03 - Store Manager (Usuário primário): Manage books, prices, inventory, low-stock notifications, promotions, and purchase records.
  STK-04 - Email Delivery Service (Stakeholder externo): Deliver low-stock and promotion notification emails requested by BECS.

Regras de negócio:
  RN-001 - Exact-title search: A book search is valid only when the search text exactly matches the book title.
  RN-002 - One copy per book per order: An order may contain no more than one copy of the same book.
  RN-003 - Member-only promotional codes: Only members may use promotional codes during checkout.
  RN-004 - Percentage-off promotions: A promotion applies a percentage reduction to an eligible order.
  RN-005 - Mutually exclusive account types: A store manager account and a customer account are mutually exclusive account types.
  RN-006 - Low-stock notification suppression: A low-stock notification is not required for a book whose notification has been disabled by the store manager.
  RN-007 - No payment processing: Card-number collection does not constitute payment authorization, charging, settlement, or money movement.
  RN-008 - Purchase-record content: Each completed purchase record must identify the purchased books, the purchaser, and the purchase date and time.
  RN-009 - Stock availability [INFERRED]: A book may be included in a completed order only when at least one copy is available in stock.

Requisitos funcionais:
  RF-001 - Customer account registration: The system shall register a customer account without requiring account verification. [Must have]
  RF-002 - Customer authentication: The system shall authenticate a customer using registered credentials. [Must have]
  RF-003 - Catalog browsing: The system shall display the available books with title, author, and price. [Must have]
  RF-004 - Exact-title search: The system shall return books whose titles exactly match the customer-provided search text. [Must have]
  RF-005 - Add book to cart: The system shall add a selected book to the customer's shopping cart. [Must have]
  RF-006 - Enforce cart quantity limit: The system shall limit each book quantity in a shopping cart to one copy. [Must have]
  RF-007 - Collect card number: The system shall collect a card number during checkout without initiating payment processing. [Must have]
  RF-008 - Record completed purchase: The system shall create a purchase record containing purchased books, purchaser identity, and completion date and time. [Must have]
  RF-009 - Generate receipt: The system shall generate a receipt after a purchase record is created. [Must have]
  RF-010 - Update stock after purchase [INFERRED]: The system shall reduce the stock quantity of each purchased book by one after purchase completion. [Must have]
  RF-011 - Member enrollment: The system shall enroll a customer as a member for promotion notifications. [Should have]
  RF-012 - Apply promotional code: The system shall apply a valid promotional code to a member's checkout total. [Should have]
  RF-013 - Manager authentication: The system shall authenticate the store manager using a manager account that is not a customer account. [Must have]
  RF-014 - Add book: The system shall allow the store manager to add a book with title, author, price, and stock quantity. [Must have]
  RF-015 - Update book price: The system shall allow the store manager to update the price of an existing book. [Must have]
  RF-016 - View stock quantity: The system shall display the current stock quantity for each book to the store manager. [Must have]
  RF-017 - Configure low-stock notifications: The system shall allow the store manager to enable or disable low-stock notifications for an individual book. [Should have]
  RF-018 - Send low-stock email: The system shall send a low-stock email to the store manager when a book with enabled notifications reaches its low-stock threshold [TBD]. [Should have]
  RF-019 - Create percentage promotion: The system shall allow the store manager to create a promotional code with a percentage-off value. [Should have]
  RF-020 - Notify members about promotion: The system shall send an email notification to every enrolled member when the store manager creates a promotion. [Should have]

Requisitos não funcionais:
  RNF-001 (Compatibility) - The system shall complete all critical customer and manager workflows in the latest two stable releases of Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari [TBD]. | Métrica: [TBD] 0 critical defects in 8 browser-version combinations.
  RNF-002 (Reliability) - The system shall maintain at least 99.5% monthly availability, excluding announced maintenance windows [TBD]. | Métrica: [TBD] Maximum 3.6 hours of unplanned downtime per calendar month.
  RNF-003 (Performance Efficiency) - The system shall return catalog browsing and exact-title search results within 2 seconds at the 95th percentile under 100 concurrent users [TBD]. | Métrica: [TBD] 95th-percentile response time of 2 seconds or less with 100 concurrent users.
  RNF-004 (Maintainability) - The system shall maintain automated test coverage of at least 80% for business-rule and inventory-management code [TBD]. | Métrica: [TBD] Line coverage of 80% or greater for the defined code scope.

Histórias de usuário:

  HU-002 - Como As a customer, quero I want to browse and search the book catalog by exact title, para so that I can find a book available for purchase.

Casos de uso:
  UC-001 - Register customer account | Ator: Prospective Customer
    1. The prospective customer enters the required registration details.
    2. The prospective customer submits the registration form.
    3. The system creates the customer account.
    4. The system displays account-creation confirmation.
  UC-002 - Search catalog by exact title | Ator: Customer
    1. The customer enters a book title in the search field.
    2. The customer submits the search.
    3. The system compares the search text with book titles using exact matching.
    4. The system displays matching books with title, author, and price.
  UC-003 - Add book to shopping cart | Ator: Customer
    1. The customer selects a book.
    2. The customer requests to add the book to the cart.
    3. The system adds one copy of the book to the cart.
    4. The system displays the updated cart.
  UC-004 - Complete checkout | Ator: Customer
    1. The customer starts checkout.
    2. The system displays the order summary.
    3. The customer enters a card number and confirms checkout.
    4. The system creates the purchase record.
    5. The system reduces stock for each purchased book.
    6. The system generates and displays the receipt.
  UC-005 - Enroll as member | Ator: Customer
    1. The customer selects membership enrollment.
    2. The system displays the membership enrollment option.
    3. The customer confirms enrollment.
    4. The system records the customer as a member.
  UC-006 - Add book to inventory | Ator: Store Manager
    1. The store manager opens the add-book function.
    2. The store manager enters the title, author, price, and stock quantity.
    3. The store manager submits the book data.
    4. The system creates the book record.
  UC-007 - View stock quantity | Ator: Store Manager
    1. The store manager opens the inventory view.
    2. The system retrieves current book stock quantities.
    3. The system displays each book with its current stock quantity.
  UC-008 - Notify manager of low stock | Ator: Store Manager
    1. The system detects that a book has reached its low-stock threshold.
    2. The system checks whether notifications are enabled for the book.
    3. The system sends a low-stock email to the store manager.
  UC-009 - Create promotion and notify members | Ator: Store Manager
    1. The store manager opens the promotion-creation function.
    2. The store manager enters a promotional code and percentage-off value.
    3. The store manager confirms promotion creation.
    4. The system creates the promotion.
    5. The system sends a promotion email to every enrolled member.

Critérios de aceite:
  CA-001 - Dado a prospective customer has entered all required registration data, quando the customer submits the registration form, então the system creates one customer account and displays a confirmation without presenting an account-verification step
  CA-002 - Dado a customer has a registered account, quando the customer submits valid registered credentials, então the system authenticates the customer and displays the customer session
  CA-003 - Dado the catalog contains an available book, quando a customer opens the catalog, então the system displays that book's title, author, and price
  CA-004 - Dado the catalog contains a book titled "Book A", quando a customer searches for "Book A", então the system displays "Book A" and does not return a book titled "Book A Revised" solely from that search
  CA-005 - Dado a customer is viewing an in-stock book not currently in the cart, quando the customer selects Add to Cart, então the system displays the selected book in the cart with quantity 1
  CA-006 - Dado a cart already contains one copy of "Book A", quando the customer requests to add "Book A" again, então the cart retains "Book A" at quantity 1
  CA-007 - Dado a customer has an in-stock cart, quando the customer enters a card number and confirms checkout, então the system accepts the card-number field and creates no payment authorization, charge, or settlement transaction
  CA-008 - Dado a customer completes checkout for "Book A", quando the system creates the purchase record, então the record contains "Book A", the customer identifier, and a completion date and time
  CA-009 - Dado a purchase record has been created, quando checkout completes, então the system displays one receipt associated with that purchase record
  CA-010 - Dado "Book A" has stock quantity 3, quando a purchase of one copy of "Book A" completes, então the system displays stock quantity 2 for "Book A"
  CA-011 - Dado a registered customer is not a member, quando the customer confirms membership enrollment, então the system records the customer as a member
  CA-012 - Dado a member has a checkout total of 100.00 and enters a valid 10% promotional code, quando the member applies the code, então the system displays a discount of 10.00 and a revised checkout total of 90.00
  CA-013 - Dado an account is registered as a customer account, quando the account is evaluated for manager authentication, então the system does not authenticate that customer account as the store manager
  CA-014 - Dado the store manager is authenticated, quando the manager submits a book with title, author, price, and stock quantity, então the system creates one catalog book record containing the submitted four values
  CA-015 - Dado the store manager is authenticated and "Book A" has price 20.00, quando the manager changes the price to 25.00, então the system displays price 25.00 for "Book A"
  CA-016 - Dado the store manager is authenticated and "Book A" has stock quantity 7, quando the manager opens the inventory view, então the system displays "Book A" with stock quantity 7
  CA-017 - Dado the store manager is authenticated and notifications are enabled for "Book A", quando the manager disables low-stock notifications for "Book A", então the system records notifications as disabled for "Book A"
  CA-018 - Dado "Book A" has low-stock notifications enabled and reaches its configured low-stock threshold [TBD], quando the threshold condition is detected, então the system submits one low-stock email notification for "Book A" to the store manager
  CA-019 - Dado the store manager is authenticated, quando the manager submits promotional code "SAVE10" with percentage-off value 10, então the system creates promotional code "SAVE10" with a 10% reduction value
  CA-020 - Dado three customers are enrolled as members, quando the store manager creates a promotion, então the system submits exactly three promotion email notifications, one for each enrolled member

Glossário:
  Book: A catalog item offered for sale, identified in BECS by at least title, author, price, and stock quantity.
  Customer: A person holding a regular account who can browse books and place orders.
  Member: A customer enrolled to receive promotion notifications and eligible to use promotional codes.
  Store Manager: The single administrative user responsible for catalog, inventory, notification, and promotion management.
  Promotional Code: A manager-created code that applies a percentage-off reduction to a member's checkout total.
  Low-stock threshold: The stock quantity at or below which a book is considered low in stock; its numeric value is [TBD].
  Purchase Record: A persistent record of a completed order containing purchased books, purchaser identity, and completion date and time.
  Receipt: The checkout confirmation generated after a purchase record is created.

Este documento é a base de conhecimento fixa (Vector Store B) do sistema de elicitação de requisitos. Ele ensina ao agente
de IA os padrões de escrita, templates, exemplos e regras de qualidade que devem ser aplicados ao analisar documentos 
de projeto.PARTE 1 — Estrutura do Documento de Especificação de Requisitos (SRS)
Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §9.6 · IEEE 830-1998 §3 · Sommerville (2016, cap. 4)
O Documento de Especificação de Requisitos de Software (SRS) é o contrato técnico que descreve o 
que o sistema deve fazer e sob quais condições de qualidade. Ele serve de referência para 
desenvolvedores, testadores, gerentes e clientes durante todo o ciclo de vida do projeto.
1.1 Artefatos Obrigatórios e sua Ordem
Um SRS completo e formal deve conter os seguintes artefatos, nesta ordem:
• ESCOPO: Define o que está DENTRO e FORA do projeto. Evita scope creep.
• STAKEHOLDERS: Lista todos os envolvidos: quem usa, quem financia, quem é afetado.
• PREMISSAS E RESTRIÇÕES: Fatos assumidos como verdadeiros e limites impostos ao projeto.
• REGRAS DE NEGÓCIO (RN): Políticas, fórmulas e condições de negócio que existem independentemente 
do software.
• REQUISITOS FUNCIONAIS (RF): O que o sistema DEVE FAZER — comportamentos, serviços, respostas a 
entradas.
• REQUISITOS NÃO FUNCIONAIS (RNF): Como o sistema deve SER — atributos de qualidade 
quantificáveis.
• HISTÓRIAS DE USUÁRIO (HU): Necessidades na perspectiva do usuário: Como [perfil], quero [ação], para
[benefício].
• CASOS DE USO (UC): Interações detalhadas ator-sistema com fluxo principal, alternativo e exceções.
• CRITÉRIOS DE ACEITE (CA): Condições testáveis em formato BDD (Dado/Quando/Então) que definem 
quando o requisito está concluído.
• GLOSSÁRIO: Termos do domínio com definição precisa para eliminar ambiguidades.
1.2 Como os Artefatos se Interconectam
Os artefatos formam uma cadeia de rastreabilidade. Cada RF deve ter origem em um STK 
(stakeholder) ou RN. Cada HU deve ter pelo menos um RF associado. Cada RF e HU devem ter pelo menos um CA. Esta rastreabilidade garante que nada seja implementado sem justificativa de 
negócio e que tudo que foi prometido seja testável.
Cadeia de rastreabilidade mínima:
STK → (RN →) RF → HU → CA

A ISO/IEC 25010:2023 define 9 características de qualidade do produto. Todo RNF deve ser 
classificado em uma dessas características. A seguir, cada característica com seus sub-atributos e 
exemplo de RNF.
1. Functional Suitability (Adequação Funcional)
 Functional Completeness — o sistema oferece todas as funções necessárias.
 Functional Correctness — as funções produzem os resultados corretos.
 Functional Appropriateness — as funções facilitam a realização das tarefas.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 1. Functional Suitability
O sistema deve calcular o imposto sobre o valor do pedido aplicando corretamente a alíquota de ICMS 
vigente para o estado de destino, conforme tabela oficial CONFAZ, com variação máxima de R$ 0,01 em 
relação ao valor de referência da Receita Estadual.
2. Performance Efficiency (Eficiência de Desempenho)
 Time Behaviour — tempo de resposta e throughput.
 Resource Utilisation — uso de CPU, memória, rede.
 Capacity — limites máximos suportados.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 2. Performance Efficiency
O sistema deve processar no mínimo 200 pedidos por minuto sob carga de 1.000 usuários simultâneos, com 
tempo de resposta inferior a 2 segundos no percentil 95.
3. Compatibility (Compatibilidade)
 Co-existence — coexiste com outros sistemas sem degradação.
 Interoperability — troca dados com outros sistemas.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 3. Compatibility
A API do sistema deve expor endpoints REST/JSON compatíveis com o padrão OpenAPI 3.0, permitindo 
integração com o ERP legado via OAuth 2.0 sem modificações no ERP.4. Interaction Capability (Capacidade de Interação) — antes 'Usabilidade'
 Appropriateness Recognisability — usuário reconhece a adequação do sistema.
 Learnability — facilidade de aprendizado.
 Operability — facilidade de operação.
 User Error Protection — proteção contra erros do usuário.
 User Engagement — interface envolvente e motivadora.
 Inclusivity — acessível a pessoas com diferentes capacidades.
 User Assistance — suporte ao usuário.
 Self-Descriptiveness — interface autoexplicativa.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 4. Interaction Capability
Um usuário sem treinamento prévio deve ser capaz de registrar seu primeiro pedido completo em até 10 
minutos. A interface deve seguir as diretrizes WCAG 2.1 nível AA.
5. Reliability (Confiabilidade)
 Faultlessness — ausência de falhas em condições normais.
 Availability — proporção de tempo em que o sistema está operacional.
 Fault Tolerance — operação correta mesmo com falhas parciais.
 Recoverability — recuperação após falha.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 5. Reliability
O sistema deve ter disponibilidade mínima de 99,5% ao mês (máx. 3,6h de downtime não planejado). Em 
caso de falha crítica, o sistema deve restaurar a operação normal em até 4 horas (RTO = 4h).

It’s not always worth taking the time to generate a complete set of requirements for an entire 
production system. Many options lie between the two extremes of continuing forever with no 
requirements documentation and reconstructing a perfect requirements set. Knowing why you’d like 
to have written requirements available lets you judge whether the cost of rebuilding all—or even 
part—of the specification is a sound investment.
Perhaps your current system is a shapeless mass of history and mystery like the one in Figure 21-2. 
Imagine that you’ve been asked to implement some new functionality in region A in this figure. 
Begin by recording the new requirements in a structured SRS or in a requirements management tool. 
When you add the new functionality, you’ll have to figure out how it interfaces to or fits in with the 
existing system. The bridges in Figure 21-2 between region A and your current system represent these 
interfaces. This analysis provides insight into the white portion of the current system, region B. In 
addition to the requirements for region A, this insight is the new knowledge you need to capture.CHAPTER 21 Enhancement and replacement projects 399
FIGURE 21-2 Adding enhancement A to an ill-documented existing system provides some visibility into the 
B area.
Rarely do you need to document the entire existing system. Focus detailed requirements efforts 
on the changes needed to meet the business objectives. If you’re replacing a system, start by 
documenting the areas prioritized as most important to achieve the business objectives or those that 
pose the highest implementation risk. Any new requirements identified during the gap analysis will 
need to be specified at the same level of precision and using the same techniques as you would for a 
new system.
Level of detail
One of the biggest challenges is determining the appropriate level of detail at which to document 
requirements gleaned from the existing system. For enhancements, defining requirements for the 
new functionality alone might be sufficient. However, you will usually benefit from documenting all of 
the functionality that closely relates to the enhancement, to ensure that the change fits in seamlessly 
(region B in Figure 21-2). You might want to create business processes, user requirements, and/or 
functional requirements for those related areas. For example, let’s say you are adding a discount code 
feature to an existing shopping cart function, but you don’t have any documented requirements for 
the shopping cart. You might be tempted to write just a single user story: “As a customer, I need to be 
able to enter a discount code so I can get the cheapest price for the product.” However, this user story 
alone lacks context, so consider capturing other user stories about shopping cart operations. That 
information could be valuable the next time you need to modify the shopping cart function.
I worked with one team that was just beginning to develop the requirements for version 2 of 
a major product with embedded software. They hadn’t done a good job on the requirements for 
version 1, which was currently being implemented. The lead BA wondered, “Is it worth going back 
to improve the SRS for version 1?” The company anticipated that this product line would be a major 
revenue generator for at least 10 years. They also planned to reuse some of the core requirements 
in several spin-off products. In this case, it made sense to improve the requirements documentation 
for version 1 because it was the foundation for all subsequent development work in this product line.

SRS described just the differences that the new version should exhibit compared to the previous 
version. Nowhere was there a description of the original system. Consequently, everyone had a 
different understanding of the current system’s capabilities. If you’re in this situation, document 
the requirements for your project more thoroughly so that all the stakeholders—both present 
and future—understand what the system does.
Expected challenges
The presence of an existing system leads to common challenges that both enhancement and 
replacement projects will face, including the following:
■ The changes made could degrade the performance to which users are accustomed.
■ Little or no requirements documentation might be available for the existing system.
■ Users who are familiar with how the system works today might not like the changes they are 
about to encounter.
■ You might unknowingly break or omit functionality that is vital to some stakeholder group.
■ Stakeholders might take this opportunity to request new functionality that seems like a good 
idea but isn’t really needed to meet the business objectives.
Even if there is existing documentation, it might not prove useful. For enhancement projects, 
the documentation might not be up to date. If the documentation doesn’t match the existing 
application’s reality, it is of limited use. For replacement systems, you also need to be wary of carrying 
forward all of the requirements, because some of the old functionality probably should not be 
migrated.
One of the major issues in replacement projects is validating that the reasons for the replacement 
are sound. There need to be justifiable business objectives for the change. When existing systems 
are being completely replaced, organizational processes might also have to change, which makes it 
harder for people to accept a new system. The change in business processes, change in the software 
system, and learning curve of a new system can disrupt current operations.

1.3 Princípios Fundamentais de Qualidade de Requisitos
Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §5.2 — Características do requisito individual
• Necessário: Existe uma necessidade real que o justifica. Sem o requisito, há uma lacuna de negócio.
• Não ambíguo: Tem uma única interpretação possível. Evitar: 'eficiente', 'fácil', 'rápido', 'amigável'.
• Verificável: Pode ser testado objetivamente com critério mensurável. 'Rápido' não é verificável; '< 2 s' é.
• Singular: Descreve uma única coisa. Nunca usar 'e' ou 'ou' para combinar dois comportamentos em um 
RF.
• Viável: Tecnicamente e financeiramente possível dentro das restrições do projeto.
• Rastreável: Tem origem (stakeholder ou RN) e destino (caso de teste) identificados.
• Completo: Contém todas as informações necessárias para implementação sem consultas adicionais.
• Consistente: Não conflita com nenhum outro requisito do documento.
• Priorizado: Tem um nível de prioridade definido (MoSCoW: Must/Should/Could/Won't).PARTE 2 — Padrões de Escrita por Artefato

projects
Most of this book describes requirements development as though you are beginning a new software 
or system development project, sometimes called a green-field project. However, many organizations 
devote much of their effort to enhancing or replacing existing information systems or building 
new releases of established commercial products. Most of the practices described in this book are 
appropriate for enhancement and replacement projects. This chapter provides specific suggestions as 
to which practices are most relevant and how to use them.
An enhancement project is one in which new capabilities are added to an existing system. 
Enhancement projects might also involve correcting defects, adding new reports, and modifying 
functionality to comply with revised business rules or needs.
A replacement (or reengineering) project replaces an existing application with a new custom-built 
system, a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) system, or a hybrid of those. Replacement projects are 
most commonly implemented to improve performance, cut costs (such as maintenance costs or 
license fees), take advantage of modern technologies, or meet regulatory requirements. If your 
replacement project will involve a COTS solution, the guidance presented in Chapter 22, “Packaged 
solution projects,” will also be helpful.
Replacement and enhancement projects face some particular requirements issues. The original 
developers who held all the critical information in their heads might be long gone. It’s tempting to 
claim that a small enhancement doesn’t warrant writing any requirements. Developers might believe 
that they don’t need detailed requirements if they are replacing an existing system’s functionality. 
The approaches described in this chapter can help you to deal with the challenges of enhancing or 
replacing an existing system to improve its ability to meet the organization’s current business needs.

fluxo_principal: 1. The prospective customer enters the required registration details.
2. The prospective customer submits the registration form.
3. The system creates the customer account.
4. The system displays account-creation confirmation.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. The submitted identifier is already registered → the system displays an identifier-in-use message; returns to step 1.

fluxo_principal: 1. The customer enters a book title in the search field.
2. The customer submits the search.
3. The system compares the search text with book titles using exact matching.
4. The system displays matching books with title, author, and price.
fluxos_alternativos: 4a. No exact title matches → the system displays a no-exact-match result.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. The search text is empty → the system requests a title before performing the search (ref. RN-001, RF-004).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The customer is viewing an available book.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The book is present in the cart with quantity one.
fluxo_principal: 1. The customer selects a book.
2. The customer requests to add the book to the cart.
3. The system adds one copy of the book to the cart.
4. The system displays the updated cart.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. The book is already in the cart → the system retains quantity one and displays the cart.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. The book has no available stock → the system does not add the book and displays an unavailable-stock message (ref. RN-009, RF-005).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The authenticated customer has a cart containing one or more in-stock books.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: A purchase record and receipt are created, and stock is updated.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No purchase record is created and stock is unchanged.
fluxo_principal: 1. The customer starts checkout.
2. The system displays the order summary.
3. The customer enters a card number and confirms checkout.
4. The system creates the purchase record.
5. The system reduces stock for each purchased book.
6. The system generates and displays the receipt.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. The customer is a member and enters a valid promotional code → the system applies the percentage reduction before confirmation.
fluxos_excecao: 3b. A cart item is out of stock → the system does not create the purchase record and displays an unavailable-stock message (ref. RN-009, RF-008).

casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The customer is recorded as a member.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: The customer's membership status is unchanged.
fluxo_principal: 1. The customer selects membership enrollment.
2. The system displays the membership enrollment option.
3. The customer confirms enrollment.
4. The system records the customer as a member.
fluxos_alternativos: 4a. The customer is already a member → the system displays the existing membership status.
fluxos_excecao: 3b. The enrollment request cannot be saved → the system displays an enrollment-failed message and does not change membership status (ref. RF-011).

em_escopo: Account creation for any visitor, with no verification process
Book search by exact title match (logged-in users)
Viewing book title, author, and price
Shopping cart with a limit of one copy per book per order
Checkout flow that collects a card number, generates a receipt, and logs the purchase
Member signup to receive promotion notifications and use promo codes at checkout
Manager login to manage inventory (add books, edit prices, view stock)
Automatic low-stock email alert to the manager, with per-book opt-out
Manager-created percentage-off promotions with automatic email to all members
fora_de_escopo: Real credit card / payment processing — deferred to a later phase
Encryption — not a priority for this version
Password recovery — not a priority for this version
Multiple manager accounts or manager roles — only one manager
Partial/fuzzy search or search by author — title search is exact-match only
Multiple copies of the same book per order — limited to one
premissas: PA-01: Only one person will operate the manager account for the store.
restricoes: REST-01 (Tecnica): The system must be usable through a normal web browser, with no exotic client-side requirements.

stakeholders.descricao: Store Manager — the single account responsible for managing inventory (add books, edit prices, view stock) and creating promotions; must never also be a regular customer account.
Visitor — anyone arriving at the site who can create an account with no verification process.
Registered User / Customer — logged-in user who can search for books, add them to a cart, and check out.
Member — a registered user who opted in to promotion notifications; the only type of user who can apply promo codes at checkout.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: A cart may contain at most one copy of each distinct book per order.
A manager account must never also function as a regular customer account.
Only members (not all registered users) can apply promo codes at checkout.
The low-stock email alert to the manager is suppressed for a given book if the manager has disabled notifications for that specific book.
Creating a new percentage-off promotion automatically triggers an email to all members.

requisitos_funcionais.descricao: The system must allow any visitor to create an account with no verification process.
The system must allow logged-in users to search for books by title using an exact match only (no partial match, no search by author).
The system must display each book's title, author, and price.
The system must allow users to add a book to their shopping cart.
The system must prevent a user from adding more than one copy of the same book to their cart in a single order.
The system must allow users to complete checkout for the items in their cart.
The system must allow a registered user to sign up as a member to receive promotion notifications.
The system must allow members to apply a promo code during checkout.
The system must provide a login for the manager, separate from customer accounts.
The system must allow the manager to add new books to the inventory.
The system must allow the manager to edit the price of existing books.
The system must allow the manager to view current stock levels.
The system must send an email notification to the manager when a book's stock is low, unless notifications are disabled for that book.
The system must allow the manager to create percentage-off promotions.
The system must automatically email all members when a new promotion is created.
The system must collect a card number during checkout without processing an actual payment.
The system must generate a receipt after checkout.
The system must log each purchase, including the item, the buyer, and the timestamp.

requisitos_nao_funcionais.descricao: The system must be usable through a standard web browser, with no exotic or non-standard client-side requirements.

historias_de_usuario.descricao: As a visitor, I want to create an account with no verification process, so that I can start using the site quickly.
As a registered user, I want to search for a book by its exact title, so that I can find the book I'm looking for.
As a registered user, I want to view a book's title, author, and price, so that I can decide whether to buy it.
As a registered user, I want to add a book to my cart, so that I can purchase it later.
As a registered user, I want to check out my cart, so that I can complete my purchase.
As a member, I want to apply a promo code at checkout, so that I can get a discount.
As the manager, I want to add new books and edit their prices, so that I can keep the catalog up to date.
As the manager, I want to be notified when a book's stock is low, so that I can restock in time.
As the manager, I want to create percentage-off promotions, so that I can attract more sales.
As a member, I want to receive an email when a new promotion is created, so that I know about current deals.

casos_de_uso.descricao: Search and Purchase Book — a logged-in user searches for a book by exact title, adds it to the cart, and completes checkout.
Manage Inventory — the manager logs in and adds new books, edits prices, or views current stock levels.
Create Promotion — the manager creates a percentage-off promotion, and the system automatically emails all members.

criterios_de_aceite.descricao: Given a logged-in user, when they search for a book title that exactly matches an existing book, then the system returns that book with its title, author, and price.
Given a user already has one copy of a book in their cart, when they try to add another copy of the same book, then the system prevents the second copy from being added.
Given a member is at checkout with a valid promo code, when they apply the code, then the system applies the corresponding discount.
Given a book's stock drops below the defined threshold and notifications are enabled for that book, when the stock update occurs, then the system sends an email to the manager.
Given the manager creates a new percentage-off promotion, when the promotion is saved, then the system automatically sends an email to all members.
